full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Provisions on Procedures for Handling Cases of National Judicial Assistance by People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), the Forms for Documents on National Judicial Assistance by People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), and the Working Rules of the Judicial Assistance Committee of the Supreme People's Court (for Trial Implementation)

Fa Fa [2019] No. 2

To: All High People's Courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; and all units of this Court:

In order to further promote the standardization of the work on national judicial assistance by people's courts and refine operational norms, this Court has formulated the Provisions on Procedures for Handling Cases of National Judicial Assistance by People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), the Forms for Documents on National Judicial Assistance by People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), and the Working Rules of the Judicial Assistance Committee of the Supreme People's Court (for Trial Implementation). The above documents are hereby issued to you for serious implementation. If any situations or issues are discovered during implementation, please promptly report them to the Office of the Judicial Assistance Committee of this Court.

January 4, 2019

Provisions on Procedures for Handling Cases of National Judicial Assistance by People's Courts (for Trial Implementation)

In order to further standardize the procedures for handling cases of national judicial assistance by people's courts, these Provisions are formulated in accordance with the Opinions on Establishing and Improving the National Judicial Assistance System (for Trial Implementation) jointly issued by the Central Political and Legal Affairs Commission of the CPC, the Ministry of Finance, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Justice, as well as the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Strengthening and Standardizing the Work on National Judicial Assistance by People's Courts, and in light of actual work circumstances.

Article 1. Cases of national judicial assistance by people's courts shall be placed on file and handled by the court that is processing the original trial, enforcement, or petition-related litigation case (hereinafter referred to as the original case). When necessary, the higher and lower courts may also provide coordinated assistance in such cases.

For cases with coordinated assistance, the higher court shall decide, based on the availability of assistance funds, to handle the case by placing it on file jointly or to assign it to the coordinated courts for separate filing and handling.

Article 2. People's courts shall publicly provide, through filing windows (litigation service centers), the internet, and other channels, forms for documents such as the notice on applying for national judicial assistance and the application registration form.

Article 3. When, during the processing of the original case, the court, upon examination, considers that the relevant person basically meets the conditions for assistance, it shall inform that person to submit an application for assistance and carry out preparatory work for filing in accordance with the guidance provided in the notice on applying and the application registration form.

If a person relevant to the original case directly submits an application for assistance without being informed, the filing department shall seek the opinions of the department handling the original case and the office of the judicial assistance committee.

Article 4. Where multiple direct victims who meet the conditions for assistance due to the same original case apply for assistance, each shall submit a separate application, and the people's court shall separately place the cases on file and provide assistance. Under special circumstances, they may be treated as a single case for assistance.

Where multiple close relatives who meet the conditions for assistance due to the death of a direct victim apply for assistance, they shall jointly submit an application, and the people's court shall treat it as a single case for assistance. Under special circumstances, separate cases may be placed on file and assistance provided. For close relatives who, without legitimate reasons, do not jointly submit an application, the people's court generally will no longer place the case on file for assistance and may inform them to seek a reasonable distribution of the assistance funds from the other close relatives.

Article 5. A person without capacity for litigation shall be represented in applying for assistance by a guardian acting as their legal representative.

The applicant for assistance or the legal representative may entrust one close relative of the applicant for assistance, a legal aid worker, or any other citizen acting without compensation who is permitted by the people's court as an agent ad litem.

Article 6. During the preparatory work for filing, the applicant for assistance may request the people's court to assist in providing relevant legal documents.

If the applicant for assistance applies for enforcement assistance, they shall submit a statement explaining the status of the property levy against the person subject to enforcement and the progress of the case enforcement. If the applicant applies for assistance related to litigation petitions, they shall submit a commitment to cease petitioning and litigation.

Article 7. After completing the preparatory work for filing in accordance with the guidance, the applicant for assistance shall submit all materials to the department handling the original case.

If the department handling the original case considers the materials complete, it shall sign an opinion on the application registration form, affix the department's seal, and, within five working days, transfer the application notice (signed and confirmed by the applicant for assistance), the application registration form, relevant supporting materials, and internal materials such as a preliminary examination report to the filing department for handling the filing procedures.

Article 8. After receiving the materials transferred from the department handling the original case, the filing department shall, if it considers them complete and correct, assign a case number within five working days, enter the relevant information into the case handling system, notify the applicant for assistance in writing or by electronic means, and promptly transfer the case to the office of the judicial assistance committee.

If the department handling the original case or the filing department considers that the application materials are incomplete or contain errors, it shall inform the applicant of all the content that needs to be supplemented or corrected at one time and specify a reasonable time limit for supplementation. If the applicant for assistance refuses to supplement or fails to do so within the specified time limit without legitimate reasons, the application for assistance shall be deemed waived, and the people's court shall not place the case on file.

Article 9. In handling cases of national judicial assistance, the people's court shall form a collegial panel composed of judges from the office of the judicial assistance committee to conduct examination and deliberation. When necessary, a collegial panel may also be formed jointly by judges from the office of the judicial assistance committee and judges from the department handling the original case for examination and deliberation.

The collegial panel shall designate one judge responsible for conducting the specific examination and drafting the examination report.

Article 10. When the collegial panel examines a case of national judicial assistance, it may ascertain the living difficulties of the applicant for assistance through methods such as in-person interviews, organizing hearings, household investigations, neighborhood inquiries, public reviews, correspondence inquiries, and information verifications.

Article 11. After examination and deliberation, the collegial panel may directly make a decision on cases within the scope of authorization of the judicial assistance committee. For cases where the opinions in the deliberation are inconsistent or the case is of significant difficulty or complexity, as well as for cases beyond the scope of authorization, the collegial panel shall submit the case to the judicial assistance committee for discussion and decision. For cases where there is significant divergence of opinion during the discussion by the judicial assistance committee, the matter may be submitted to the judicial committee for discussion and decision.

Article 12. The people's court shall conclude the handling of a case of national judicial assistance within ten working days from the date of filing, and at the latest within two months. Under special circumstances, with the approval of the chairperson of the judicial assistance committee, the period may be extended by an additional month.

In any of the following circumstances, the corresponding time shall not be counted in the handling period:

(1) Where the applicant for assistance needs to supplement materials;
(2) Where it is necessary to obtain evidence materials from external entities;
(3) Where a response or interpretation on a specific matter is required from the national judicial assistance leading group or a higher people's court.

Article 13. The handling of a case shall be suspended in any of the following circumstances:

(1) The applicant for assistance is unable to cooperate with the examination due to force majeure;
(2) The applicant for assistance loses capacity for litigation and no legal representative has yet been appointed;
(3) Other circumstances under which the people's court considers that the handling should be suspended.

Upon the elimination of the cause for suspension, the handling shall resume.

Article 14. The handling of a case shall be terminated in any of the following circumstances:

(1) The living difficulties of the applicant for assistance have been eliminated during the period of handling the case;
(2) The applicant for assistance refuses to accept the amount of assistance decided by the people's court;
(3) Other circumstances under which the people's court considers that the handling should be terminated.

Article 15. When the people's court makes a decision on a case of national judicial assistance, it shall issue a written decision on national judicial assistance, affixed with the seal of the people's court.

The written decision on national judicial assistance shall include the following:

(1) The basic information of the applicant for assistance;
(2) The application, facts, and reasons submitted by the applicant for assistance;
(3) The facts and evidence found, the legal provisions applied, and the reasons for the decision;
(4) The outcome of the decision.

Article 16. The people's court shall serve legal documents such as the written decision on national judicial assistance to the applicant for assistance.

Article 17. For cases where the Supreme People's Court decides to grant assistance, the amount of assistance shall be determined based on the average monthly wage of workers in the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where the court with jurisdiction over the original case is located, for the preceding year. For cases where other people's courts at various levels decide to grant assistance, the amount of assistance shall be determined based on the average monthly wage of workers in the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where that court is located, for the preceding year.

If the average monthly wage of workers for the preceding year has not yet been published at the time the people's court makes the assistance decision, the most recent published average monthly wage for workers in that year shall apply.

Article 18. If the applicant for assistance has preliminary evidence demonstrating that their living difficulties are particularly urgent, the department handling the original case may propose a suggestion for advance assistance and submit it directly to the office of the judicial assistance committee for expedited approval.

The amount of advance assistance shall generally not exceed three times the average monthly wage of workers in the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for the preceding year. When necessary, it may be relaxed to up to six times.

After providing advance assistance, the people's court shall place the case on file for supplementary examination. If, upon examination, the person is found to meet the conditions for assistance, the court shall decide to make up the balance of the assistance funds; if, upon examination, the person is found not to meet the conditions for assistance, the court shall decide not to grant assistance and shall recover the assistance funds already distributed.

Article 19. If a decision is made to grant assistance, the office of the judicial assistance committee shall, within seven working days, handle the fund requisition procedures in accordance with relevant financial regulations, and within two working days after the assistance funds are in place, notify the applicant for assistance to complete the fund collection procedures.

Article 20. Assistance funds shall generally be distributed promptly and in a lump sum. Under special circumstances, a plan for deferred or installment distribution shall be proposed, and with the approval of the chairperson of the judicial assistance committee, the funds may be distributed in installments or on a deferred basis.

Article 21. When distributing assistance funds, the people's court shall assign two or more handlers, including at least one person from the office of the judicial assistance committee. The handlers shall explain to the applicant for assistance the nature of the assistance funds, the reasons for granting assistance, and the legal consequences of fraudulently obtaining assistance funds, and guide the applicant to fill out and sign the national judicial assistance fund distribution form for confirmation.

When the people's court deems it necessary, it may invite staff from the village (residents') committee in the applicant's registered domicile or habitual residence, or from the applicant's employer, to witness the distribution of the assistance funds.

Article 22. Assistance funds shall generally be distributed by bank transfer. Under special circumstances, with the approval of the chairperson of the judicial assistance committee, distribution may also be made in cash, provided that necessary audio and video recordings are preserved.

Article 23. In light of the specific circumstances of the applicant for assistance, the people's court may entrust civil affairs departments, township people's governments or sub-district offices, village (residents') committees, or the applicant's employer, among other organizations, to distribute the assistance funds.

Article 24. After the applicant for assistance receives assistance, if the case has not yet been concluded in enforcement, enforcement shall continue. If subsequent amounts are recovered from enforcement and the living difficulties of the applicant for assistance have been substantially alleviated or eliminated, the assistance funds already distributed shall be deducted from the enforcement proceeds and returned to the assistance fund account for revolving use.

After the applicant for assistance receives assistance, if the applicant agrees to conclude the enforcement case, the uncollected enforcement amounts shall be treated as special claims to be separately registered and managed, and enforcement shall be conducted separately. The amounts recovered from enforcement shall be returned to the assistance fund account for revolving use.

Fraudulently obtained assistance funds and assistance funds provided for petition-related litigation where the commitment to cease petitioning is violated shall be recovered and returned to the assistance fund account for revolving use.

Article 25. The handling of cases of national judicial assistance by people's courts shall be subject to the supervision and guidance of the national judicial assistance leading group and the judicial assistance committee of the higher people's court.

Article 26. These Provisions shall be interpreted by the Supreme People's Court. With the consent of the Supreme People's Court, the High People's Courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region may, on the basis of these Provisions and in light of the actual circumstances of their jurisdictions, formulate implementing rules.

Article 27. These Provisions shall take effect on February 1, 2019.

Forms for Documents on National Judicial Assistance by People's Courts (for Trial Implementation)

Forms for Documents on National Judicial Assistance by People's Courts (for Trial Implementation) 1

Notice on Applying for National Judicial Assistance by a People's Court

(To be used for informing applicants for assistance of relevant provisions)

For the purpose of facilitating an understanding of the current national judicial assistance policies and regulations, applying for assistance lawfully and reasonably, and effectively preparing supporting materials, this Notice on Applying is formulated in accordance with the Opinions on Establishing and Improving the National Judicial Assistance System (for Trial Implementation) jointly issued by the Central Political and Legal Affairs Commission of the CPC, the Ministry of Finance, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Justice, the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Strengthening and Standardizing the Work on National Judicial Assistance by People's Courts, and the Provisions on Procedures for Handling Cases of National Judicial Assistance by People's Courts (for Trial Implementation). Applicants for assistance are requested to carefully read (or listen to) these contents and confirm by signing.

I. Basic Conditions and Court Accepting the Case

(1) In the course of trial, enforcement, or petition-related litigation work, people's courts may take one-time supplementary relief measures for parties or other relevant persons whose rights have been infringed and who are facing urgent living difficulties, provided that the circumstances specified in the aforementioned Opinions are met.

(2) Cases of national judicial assistance by people's courts shall be placed on file and handled by the court that is processing the original trial, enforcement, or petition-related litigation case (hereinafter referred to as the original case). When necessary, higher and lower courts may provide coordinated assistance. For cases with coordinated assistance, the higher court shall decide, based on the availability of assistance funds, to handle the case by placing it on file jointly or to assign it to the coordinated courts for separate filing and handling.

II. Circumstances for Granting or Denying Assistance

(1) If a person relevant to the original case applies for national judicial assistance due to urgent living difficulties, and meets any of the following circumstances, assistance shall be granted:

1. The victim of a criminal offense has suffered serious injury or severe disability as a result of the crime, and due to the death of the perpetrator or lack of capacity to pay compensation, cannot obtain compensation through litigation, resulting in living difficulties;
2. The victim of a criminal offense is in a life-threatening condition as a result of the crime, urgently needs medical treatment, and cannot afford the medical treatment costs;
3. The victim of a criminal offense has died as a result of the crime, and due to the death of the perpetrator or lack of capacity to pay compensation, close relatives who primarily relied on the victim's income for their livelihood cannot obtain compensation through litigation, resulting in living difficulties;
4. The victim of a criminal offense has suffered substantial property losses as a result of the crime, and due to the death of the perpetrator or lack of capacity to pay compensation, cannot obtain compensation through litigation, resulting in living difficulties;
5. A whistleblower, witness, or expert evaluator has been subjected to retaliation for reporting, testifying, or conducting evaluations, resulting in personal injury or substantial property losses, and cannot obtain compensation through litigation, resulting in living difficulties;
6. A person claiming maintenance, support, or child support payments, where the person subject to enforcement lacks the capacity to perform, causing the applicant for enforcement to fall into living difficulties;
7. A person who has suffered personal injury due to a civil tort such as a road traffic accident, cannot obtain compensation through litigation, and the victim falls into living difficulties;
8. Other persons whom the people's court deems, based on actual circumstances, to need assistance.

For a person filing a petition related to litigation, if their claims have a certain degree of reasonableness but are difficult to resolve through legal channels, and they are in living difficulties, and are willing to cease petitioning and litigation upon receiving national judicial assistance, they may be granted assistance by reference to this Opinion.

(2) If a person relevant to the original case falls under any of the following circumstances, assistance shall generally not be granted:

1. The person bears significant fault for the occurrence of the case;
2. Without legitimate reasons, the person refuses to cooperate in ascertaining the facts of the case;
3. The person has made false statements or forged evidence, obstructing litigation;
4. During trial or enforcement, the person voluntarily waived claims for civil compensation or refused compensation from the infringer or their close relatives;
5. The living difficulties are not caused by the facts of the case;
6. The person has already received reasonable compensation or assistance through social relief measures;
7. The applicant for assistance is a legal person or other organization;
8. Other circumstances where assistance should not be granted.

III. Method of Application and Required Materials

(1) When, during the processing of the original case, the court, upon examination, considers that the relevant person basically meets the conditions for assistance, it shall inform that person to submit an application for assistance and carry out preparatory work for filing in accordance with the guidance provided in this Notice on Applying and the application registration form.

If a person relevant to the original case directly submits an application for assistance without being informed, the person shall, after the people's court confirms that the person basically meets the conditions for assistance, proceed with the preparatory work for filing in accordance with the guidance provided in this Notice on Applying and the application registration form.

(2) When an applicant for assistance submits an application for national judicial assistance, the applicant shall fill out the standard application registration form or submit a separate application letter for assistance, and provide relevant materials, mainly including: legal documents of the original case; identity documents of the applicant; identity documents and powers of attorney of the agent; materials proving actual losses (consequences of harm); materials proving the income and assets of the applicant and family members, and living difficulties; an explanation of whether compensation, indemnity, or other assistance has already been obtained; a commitment to cease petitioning and litigation upon receiving judicial assistance; and other relevant materials. If the corresponding materials cannot be provided, the reasons shall be stated.

(3) Proof of living difficulties for the applicant for assistance mainly refers to documents issued by the village (residents') committee in the applicant's registered domicile or habitual residence, or by the applicant's employer, concerning the applicant's family size, labor capacity, employment status, family income, and other circumstances.

IV. Basis for Determining the Amount of Assistance and Advance Assistance System

(1) For cases where the Supreme People's Court decides to grant assistance, the amount of assistance shall be determined based on the average monthly wage of workers in the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where the court with jurisdiction over the original case is located, for the preceding year. For cases where other people's courts at various levels decide to grant assistance, the amount of assistance shall be determined based on the average monthly wage of workers in the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where that court is located, for the preceding year. If the average monthly wage of workers for the preceding year has not yet been published at the time the people's court makes the assistance decision, the most recent published average monthly wage for workers in that year shall apply.

(2) If the applicant for assistance has preliminary evidence demonstrating that their living difficulties are particularly urgent, the applicant may apply for advance assistance through the department handling the original case. The people's court will conduct expedited approval based on the circumstances. The amount of advance assistance shall generally not exceed three times the average monthly wage of workers in the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for the preceding year. When necessary, it may be relaxed to up to six times.

V. Related Obligations and Legal Liability

(1) After the applicant for assistance receives assistance, if the people's court subsequently recovers from the person subject to enforcement compensation or other amounts due for enforcement, the assistance funds already distributed shall be deducted from the enforcement proceeds.

(2) If the applicant for assistance fraudulently obtains assistance funds by providing false materials or other means, the people's court shall recover such funds; if the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued according to law.

(3) If an applicant for assistance related to petition-related litigation receives assistance funds and subsequently violates the commitment to cease petitioning and litigation, the people's court shall recover the assistance funds.

I have [read / listened to] the above contents and fully understand their meaning. I will strictly comply with the provisions of the Opinions, properly fill out the National Judicial Assistance Application Registration Form of the People's Court, carefully prepare the relevant supporting materials, and file an application for assistance lawfully and reasonably.

Applicant for assistance: XXX (signature and fingerprint)

XXXX year XX month XX day

[Explanation]

1. This form is prepared in accordance with Article 8 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Strengthening and Regulating the State Judicial Assistance Work of People's Courts and Article 2 of the Procedural Rules for Handling State Judicial Assistance Cases of People's Courts (for Trial Implementation). It is used for people's courts to explain to persons who basically meet the conditions for assistance the current state judicial assistance policies and regulations, and to standardize the filing of assistance applications and the preparation of supporting materials.

2. "Proof of actual loss (consequences of damage)" refers to losses suffered due to infringement of personal or property rights, including but not limited to medical diagnosis conclusions, judicial appraisal opinions, expense documents, death certificates, etc.

3. The notice of matters requiring attention confirmed by the assistance applicant's signature shall be attached to the case file.

【Explanation】

1. This form is prepared in accordance with Articles 8 and 9 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Strengthening and Regulating the State Judicial Assistance Work of People's Courts and Articles 2, 3, 6, and 7 of the Procedural Rules for Handling State Judicial Assistance Cases of People's Courts (for Trial Implementation). It is used for assistance applicants to file applications and for people's courts to register applications and guide applicants in preparing for case filing.

2. This registration form has integrated and covered the essential elements of the "Application for State Judicial Assistance" and has a certain guiding function. Therefore, after the assistance applicant fills in the relevant content as prompted, prepares the relevant supporting materials, signs, and affixes a fingerprint, submission to the court is equivalent to submitting a written assistance application. If the assistance applicant's form is filled out improperly or the supporting materials are incomplete, the registering court shall provide explanations and necessary guidance.

3. If the applicant does not fill out the form but separately submits an "Application for State Judicial Assistance" and related materials, the staff of the registering court shall guide the applicant to transcribe the relevant content (may be summarized as necessary) into the form.

4. In accordance with the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Case Numbers of People's Courts, the case number assigned by the case filing department, i.e., the underlined portion in "(XXXX) ... Si Jiu X No.", specifically falls into seven categories: Si Jiu Xing (judicial relief criminal), Si Jiu Min (judicial relief civil), Si Jiu Xing (judicial relief administrative), Si Jiu Pei (judicial relief compensation), Si Jiu Zhi (judicial relief enforcement), Si Jiu Fang (judicial relief petition), and Si Jiu Ta (judicial relief other).

5. This registration form shall be attached to the case file.

People's Court State Judicial Assistance Document Format (for Trial Implementation) 3

XXXX People's Court

Notice of Acceptance of Case

(For People's Court to Accept Application for State Judicial Assistance)

(XXXX) ... Si Jiu X No.

XXX (Name of Assistance Applicant):

You filed an application for state judicial assistance with this court on XXXX, XX, XX. Upon review, your application meets the conditions for case filing, and this court has decided to accept the case for filing. The relevant matters are hereby notified as follows:

1. This case shall be reviewed and handled by the Office of the Judicial Assistance Commission of this court. Contact person of the office: ..., Contact telephone: ..., Contact address: ... .

2. During the review period of this case, you shall actively cooperate with the work of the Office of the Judicial Assistance Commission of this court; otherwise, it shall be deemed as abandonment of the application, and this court will conclude the case.

... (If there are other matters, they may continue to be specified).

This is hereby notified.

XXXX, XX, XX

(Court Seal)

【Explanation】

1. This form is prepared in accordance with Article 8 of the Procedural Rules for Handling State Judicial Assistance Cases of People's Courts (for Trial Implementation). It is used for the people's court to notify the assistance applicant in writing after case filing.

2. If it is decided to notify in writing, this notice shall be served on the assistance applicant; the signed draft of the notice and the service receipt shall be attached to the case file.

People's Court State Judicial Assistance Document Format (for Trial Implementation) 4

XXXX People's Court

Notice of Hearing

(For People's Court to Notify Assistance Applicant to Attend Hearing)

(XXXX) ... Si Jiu X No.

XXX (Name of Assistance Applicant):

Regarding your application for state judicial assistance, this court has scheduled a hearing at XX:XX on XXXX, XX, XX at (location). Please attend on time.

This is hereby notified.

XXXX, XX, XX

(Court Seal)

【Explanation】

1. This form is prepared in accordance with Article 10 of the Procedural Rules for Handling State Judicial Assistance Cases of People's Courts (for Trial Implementation). It is used for the people's court to notify the assistance applicant to attend a hearing.

2. The content and format of the hearing may refer to the provisions on hearings for self-compensation cases.

3. This notice shall be served on the assistance applicant; the signed draft of the notice and the service receipt shall be attached to the case file.

In summary, in accordance with Article 12 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Strengthening and Regulating the State Judicial Assistance Work of People's Courts and Article 15 of the Procedural Rules for Handling State Judicial Assistance Cases of People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), the decision is as follows:

(First scenario: if it is determined that the assistance conditions are met)

(Second scenario: if it is determined that the assistance conditions are not met or that there are circumstances for non-assistance)

1. It is used for the people's court to decide whether to grant judicial assistance.

2. This decision shall be served on the assistance applicant; the signed draft of the decision and the service receipt shall be attached to the case file.

3. If a decision is made to suspend or terminate the handling of the case, reference may be made to this form, but the title "State Judicial Assistance Decision" in the document header shall be correspondingly amended to "Decision", and other content shall also be adjusted accordingly.

Working Rules of the Judicial Assistance Commission of the Supreme People's Court (for Trial Implementation)

In order to standardize the work of the Judicial Assistance Commission of this court and fully leverage its functional role, these Rules are formulated in accordance with the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Strengthening and Regulating the State Judicial Assistance Work of People's Courts and relevant provisions, and in light of actual work circumstances.

Article 1 The duties of the Judicial Assistance Commission of this court are:

(1) To discuss and decide on major, difficult, and complex judicial assistance cases of this court. Cases where the proposed assistance amount exceeds thirty-six times the average monthly salary of employees in the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where the court with original jurisdiction over the case is located for the previous year, cases that are major, difficult, or complex, or where the collegiate bench has significant differences of opinion, as well as cases that the Chairperson or Vice Chairperson considers necessary to submit for discussion, shall be discussed and decided by the Judicial Assistance Commission.

(2) To discuss and decide on policy documents and guiding opinions on the state judicial assistance work of people's courts.

(3) To summarize the state judicial assistance work of people's courts, submit work reports to the State Judicial Assistance Leading Group, and supervise and guide the state judicial assistance work of local people's courts at all levels.

(4) To discuss and decide on other major matters concerning the state judicial assistance work of people's courts.

Article 2 The Judicial Assistance Commission shall implement a regular meeting system based on actual work circumstances. When necessary, meetings may be convened temporarily upon the proposal of the Chairperson.

Meetings of the Judicial Assistance Commission shall require the attendance of more than half of its members.

Article 3 Members of the Judicial Assistance Commission shall attend meetings on time. If unable to attend a meeting due to a valid reason, the member shall timely request leave from the meeting convener.

Article 4 Meetings of the Judicial Assistance Commission shall be chaired by the Chairperson, or by a Vice Chairperson delegated by the Chairperson.

Article 5 The topics for discussion by the Judicial Assistance Commission shall be determined by the Chairperson or the Vice Chairperson.

Meeting materials shall be sent to each member no later than one day prior to the meeting.

The handler of a judicial assistance case or the handler of other topics shall attend the meeting as a non-voting participant, make a report, and answer questions raised by members.

Article 6 The Judicial Assistance Commission shall practice democratic centralism. A decision of the Judicial Assistance Commission must be approved by more than half of its members to be adopted. The opinions of the minority shall be recorded in the minutes.

Documents related to matters decided by the Judicial Assistance Commission shall be signed by the meeting convener.

Article 7 If, after discussion by the Judicial Assistance Commission, opinions are significantly divergent, the Chairperson may, in accordance with relevant procedures, submit the matter to the Adjudication Committee for discussion.

The Judicial Assistance Commission shall implement the decisions of the Adjudication Committee.

Article 8 Matters discussed and decided by the Judicial Assistance Commission shall be recorded in meeting minutes, which shall be attached to the case file for future reference after approval by the meeting convener.

Article 9 An Office shall be established under the Judicial Assistance Commission, with the functions exercised by the Office of the Compensation Commission of this court. Its main responsibilities are:

(1) To handle the daily affairs of the state judicial assistance work of this court.

(2) To implement the resolutions of the Judicial Assistance Commission.

(3) To handle judicial assistance cases of this court. For judicial assistance cases where the proposed assistance amount is less than thirty-six times the average monthly salary of employees in the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where the court with original jurisdiction over the case is located for the previous year, the Office shall, upon authorization, make a decision directly in the name of the Judicial Assistance Commission of this court. For judicial assistance cases specified in Article 1, paragraph (1) of these Rules, after discussion by the collegiate bench, the Office shall request the Chairperson to submit the matter to the Judicial Assistance Commission for discussion.

(4) To handle the meeting affairs of the Judicial Assistance Commission, including meeting preparation, meeting minutes, collation and archiving of meeting materials, etc.

(5) Other matters requiring handling.

Article 10 Members of the Judicial Assistance Commission and other persons attending the meeting as non-voting participants shall comply with confidentiality provisions and shall not disclose the discussions of the Judicial Assistance Commission.

Article 11 These Rules shall come into effect as of the date of promulgation.
